long_biography.plain_text:
Perotti entered Azimut while finishing an economics degree in Turin. He became an executive three years later, joined the Azimut-Benetti board and eventually led its main Azimut division. In 2005 he left to acquire a majority of Sanlorenzo, then became chief executive and later chairman, building the Italian yard into an international luxury-vessel group.

Sanlorenzo listed in Milan in 2019, but control remained with Perotti. A subsequent reorganisation placed most shares in Ocean, held through the Perotti family's Holding Happy Life, while leaving him ultimate controller; Sanlorenzo also identifies him as chairman and chief executive. His children Cecilia and Cesare sit on the board, with operating roles at Nautor Swan and Sanlorenzo respectively. The group's shipyards, brands, subsidiaries and inventory remain corporate assets rather than Perotti's direct personal property.
